title: Synergy of strength–ductility in HfMoTaTiZr refractory high entropy alloy through Cr addition

recollection.starting_material: The study began with a refractory high‐entropy alloy composed of Hf, Mo, Ta, Ti, and Zr.
recollection.intervention: Chromium (Cr) was added to the base alloy in controlled amounts to modify its composition.
recollection.structure: The Cr addition resulted in a modified microstructure—likely a refined dual-phase or a more homogeneous body‐centered cubic (BCC) matrix with fine precipitates introduced by the Cr—that was not present in the Cr-free alloy.
recollection.mechanism: The proposed mechanism is that Cr stabilizes secondary phases or induces microstructural refinement. This in turn promotes a better balance between dislocation motion and grain boundary strengthening, leading to a synergistic improvement in both strength and ductility.
recollection.results: While I do not recall the exact figures, the paper reported a marked improvement in mechanical properties. For example, the yield strength might have increased by approximately 20–30% while the ductility (related to uniform elongation) was maintained or even enhanced by roughly 10–20% relative to the original alloy. (This description is a best guess based on typical outcomes in similar studies.)

score.note: Correctly identifies Cr addition, but only at the level revealed by the title and omits the 4.2 at.% amount. The response generically anticipates a BCC-plus-secondary-phase microstructure but misses the specific reticulated Cr₂(Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta) Laves-phase network. Its mechanism is generic and partly incorrect, omitting Cr-induced lattice distortion/dislocation hardening and crack hindrance by the reticulated Laves phase. Reported percentage changes are speculative and do not recall the actual 1750.6 MPa yield strength, 14.0% fracture strain, 3.8% Laves fraction, or 535.8 HV0.3 hardness.
